summary: Focused independent review of the updated Release Intelligence v2.0.0-GA GOLDEN BUILD ZIP SHA256 00f627c9f9e66a21694e51a8444fa01f634219431c61c8a27ea319e99da1fe86. All 30 packaged files byte-match source. The identified append-editor issue is fixed: effective-year latestMonths supplies only the newest entry, older same-month entries remain separately visible, and unchanged latest text does not publish again. Engineer mapping confirmation now binds to the complete reference configuration, including tabs, and a tab-only change requires reconfirmation. Fresh status-dependent enums, goal/mapping/Path-to-Green publication checks, exact GUS write verification, and newest-first append-only preservation remain in place. Shared schema validates the new fields and protects them in journal conflict tracking. Independently executed four targeted reference, append-preservation, and publish tests successfully. No blocking issues remain. Overall application risk remains High under the existing rubric assessment.
caveats: Newest-first append-only publication intentionally supersedes the previous oldest-first replacement policy. Existing historical bytes remain unchanged; the first recognized entry for a month is treated as its newest source entry.

Authenticated production Google Sheets integration is unverified, and the supplied private sheet export is inaccessible without authentication. No stale sheet snapshot is used; publication requires an authoritative GUS mapping or an explicit engineer mapping/confirmed-none tied to the full current reference.
Engineer-confirmed mapping is a declared fallback, not verification of the live fiscal-year sheet. Any reference URL, year, or tab change requires reconfirmation.

Fresh prechecks and exact post-write verification reduce races but do not make all host writes atomic. Shared Review Status, reference settings, mapping confirmations, and Path-to-Green changes retain underlying host concurrency limits.

Current goal/mapping/recovery gates can intentionally prevent generation or publication until required GUS data or explicit confirmations are supplied. AI checks remain heuristic; source facts, risk-first ordering, historical timing, and KPI interpretation still require human review.

Existing Slack prepare/copy-only and native-paste limitations, usage completeness, preview caching/cancellation, journal growth, revision conflicts, host/catalog/history limits, AllUsers sharing, and unavailable live list-column metadata caveats remain.

This was a fast focused source/artifact review with four independently executed targeted tests. The implementing agent reported ten workflow tests, four targeted AI tests, and the combined browser regression passed, including duplicate-month editor preservation and unchanged-save behavior. No full suite was run; actual production model, authenticated Google host integration, hosted-browser behavior, remote publication, and golden-tag movement were not independently verified.
